subject: Re: MSA & Order Form — uptime framework and maintenance runbook
messages:
From: Elena Marcos <elena@orioncloud.com>
To: marissa_cole@redwood.com
Cc: procurement@orioncloud.com
Date: Fri, 09 Oct 2026 08:12:00 -0700
Subject: OrionCloud MSA redlines — uptime and maintenance

Marissa,

Thanks for the quick turnaround on the MSA. Our legal and SRE teams reviewed the SLA appendix and flagged a few items we need to resolve before procurement can sign:

- Target uptime: we expect 99.99% across our primary US region.
- Maintenance window: the current draft allows a 6-hour monthly blackout. We'd like to limit planned maintenance to 3 hours per month or require rolling, per-az windows.
- Response times: P1 15 min acknowledgement, P2 2 hours.
- Service credits: need a clearer, tiered credit schedule and a cap tied to monthly fees.

I've attached a short change request with our preferred wording and rationale (Orion_Change_Request_v1.pdf). Can you loop in legal and SRE so we can converge on definitions (what constitutes an outage vs. maintenance) and measurement methodology?

Best,
Elena
Elena Marcos
Head of Procurement, OrionCloud

Attachment: Orion_Change_Request_v1.pdf (stub)

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Elena Marcos <elena@orioncloud.com>
Cc: kimberly_park@redwood.com, rishi_malhotra@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 09 Oct 2026 11:45:00 -0400
Subject: Re: OrionCloud MSA redlines — uptime and maintenance

Elena —

Thanks for the detailed note and the change request. We've reviewed it internally with product and wanted to propose a compromise to move things forward quickly:

- Uptime: Redwood's baseline for Dedicated and Hosted tiers is 99.95% measured monthly per-region. We can add a contractual clause committing to a 99.99% target for the primary region if Orion agrees to: (a) an initial stabilization period of 90 days post-cutover, and (b) a quarterly improvement plan tied to observability KPIs.

- Maintenance windows: we can limit any single planned maintenance to 3 hours per region and pledge rolling AZ maintenance so customer impact is minimized. We do need a 48-hour notice for standard maintenance and a 10-business-day notice for major upgrades (schema changes, runtime upgrades).

- Response times: proposed as P1 acknowledgement within 30 minutes (on-call triage), P1 mitigation SLA to be defined by ops runbook, P2 acknowledgement within 4 hours. We can bind mitigation timelines for P1 in the Order Form for an additional support commitment.

- Service credits: propose a tiered credit schedule (e.g., <99.95 = 10% monthly credit; <99.90 = 25%), with an annual cap of credits equal to 6 months of subscription fees.

I've attached a draft with inline markups (proposed-sla-markup.docx). Kimberly and Rishi — any legal/finance constraints here I should be aware of before I send back to Elena?

Next step: if Orion is OK with stabilization period + improvement plan, we can proceed to redline the Order Form and lock the credit cap. Thinking a short sync early next week would help.

Thanks,
Marissa
Marissa Cole
Director, Strategic Accounts | Redwood Inference

Attachment: proposed-sla-markup.docx (stub)

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: marissa_cole@redwood.com
Cc: rishi_malhotra@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 09 Oct 2026 14:10:00 -0400
Subject: Re: OrionCloud MSA redlines — legal redlines and measurement definitions

Marissa / Rishi —

I've reviewed Marissa's proposed compromise and added the following legal redlines and clarifications for the Order Form / SLA appendix:

1) Definition of "Downtime" and "Availability"
   - Downtime should exclude transient pod/container restarts or scaling events that do not result in user-impacting errors lasting longer than two minutes aggregated per incident.
   - Availability will be measured per-region using aggregated successful request rate across the public inference endpoint (we'll link to the telemetry query).

2) Measurement window and dispute process
   - Monthly measurement, with Redwood providing raw telemetry and a 14-day dispute window. Either party may raise an adjudication request; if unresolved, the parties will engage an agreed third-party auditor (SOC2 or equivalent) — cost split to be negotiated.

3) Credits and cap
   - Cap credits to a maximum of six (6) months' subscription fees per 12-month period. Remove language that permits unlimited stacking across products.

4) Maintenance notice and emergency carveouts
   - Standard maintenance: 48 hours' notice.
   - Major upgrade (runtime or model change): 10 business days' notice.
   - Emergency maintenance: Redwood may perform emergency maintenance without notice when needed to protect security or integrity; such events will be documented and reported monthly.

5) Security evidence
   - For Orion's procurement ask on SOC2, we will provide the latest Type II report via an NDA if not already shared — attach link in the final Order Form.

I've attached a tracked-changes doc with exact clause wording (redlines_sla_track_changes.docx). Overall these redlines are commercially reasonable and protect Redwood from open-ended credit exposure while providing Orion with measurement transparency.

-Kim
Kimberly Park
Senior Counsel, Contracts & Privacy | Redwood Inference

Attachment: redlines_sla_track_changes.docx (stub)

From: Elena Marcos <elena@orioncloud.com>
To: marissa_cole@redwood.com
Cc: procurement@orioncloud.com
Date: Mon, 12 Oct 2026 09:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: MSA & Order Form — uptime framework and maintenance runbook

Marissa / Kim —

Appreciate the rapid review and the proposed trade-offs. A few comments from Orion's SRE and procurement teams:

- Uptime: Orion's preference remains 99.99% for our primary region. Given Redwood's stabilization ask, we can accept 99.95 for the first 90 days with a hard commitment to 99.99 thereafter provided the improvement milestones are met each quarter. We also want a remediation plan if milestones are missed (accelerated credits or engineering engagement).

- Response times: Orion can accept the 30-minute acknowledgement for P1 as long as mitigation SLAs and escalation paths are documented. For P2, we need a 4-hour acknowledgement and a P2 mitigation target of 48 hours for regression severity.

- Maintenance: 3-hour per-region window with rolling AZ approach is acceptable. We'll request that routine maintenance windows be scheduled outside our peak times (we will provide our peak calendar).

- Credits: the cap of six months is acceptable if we have the remediation/engineering engagement clause and visibility into telemetry (read-only dashboards).

Attached is the security questionnaire procurement requested (orion-security-questionnaire.xlsx). Please confirm SOC2 access method (NDA or secure portal).

If you can incorporate Kim's redlines and add the stabilization milestones + remediation language, we can move to a final redline on the Order Form and target signature by end of quarter.

Thanks,
Elena
Elena Marcos
Head of Procurement, OrionCloud

Attachment: orion-security-questionnaire.xlsx (stub)

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Elena Marcos <elena@orioncloud.com>
Cc: kimberly_park@redwood.com, rishi_malhotra@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 12 Oct 2026 11:03:00 -0400
Subject: Re: MSA & Order Form — uptime framework and maintenance runbook

Elena —

Thanks for the confirmation and the questionnaire. Action items / agreed points to include in the next redline:

1) Uptime: 99.95% during 90-day stabilization window; 99.99% target thereafter tied to quarterly milestones. Include a remediation path (increased engineering support and step-up credits) if milestones are missed.
2) Measurement: monthly, per-region telemetry export + 14-day dispute window. We will provision a read-only dashboard for Orion's SREs.
3) Maintenance: 3-hour per-region planned window, rolling AZs, 48-hour notice for standard maintenance, 10 business days for major upgrades, emergency carveouts documented.
4) Response times: P1 ack 30 min, P1 mitigation engagement in ops runbook; P2 ack 4 hours, mitigation target 48 hours.
5) Service credits: tiered schedule with a maximum cap of six months' fees per 12-month period.
6) Security evidence: Kimberly will share the SOC2 Type II via secure portal / NDA.

Next steps: Kimberly will incorporate legal wording into the tracked doc. Rishi and I will prepare a short commercial addendum describing the stabilization milestones and remediation engagement. I'll schedule a 30-minute sync for Wed 10/14 at 09:30 PT to walk Orion through the runbook language and the dashboard.

If that timing works, I'll send a calendar invite and a DocuSign stub for the Order Form separation (per procurement's note).

Thanks all — looking forward to closing this quickly.

Best,
Marissa
Marissa Cole
Director, Strategic Accounts | Redwood Inference
